questions.q: Match each function of prices to its meaning.
pairs: Limits demand for a scarce good
Carries information to buyers and sellers
questions.why: Prices do all three at once.

questions.q: In a market economy, the question "for whom?" is answered mainly by:
questions.why: Goods go to those with the income to pay for them.

questions.q: Rents rise in a city. Which is the signalling function at work?
options: Builders learn that more homes are wanted there
Some people can no longer afford to live there
questions.why: A rising price tells producers that consumers want more.

questions.q: The price mechanism is called impersonal because it responds to ability to pay, whoever the buyer is.
questions.why: It treats all spending alike, which is both a strength and a weakness.

questions.q: Which is the best argument against a market for blood?
options: It changes a gift into a sale, and alters the incentives of donors
questions.why: Introducing a price can change the nature of the activity.

questions.q: Explain how a rise in the price of a good can help to allocate resources.

ideas.label: It rations the good, or signals that consumers want more
It gives firms an incentive to shift resources into making it

questions.model: A higher price rations the good and signals that consumers want more. Higher profits give firms an incentive to move resources into making it.
questions.why: Think about what the price tells people and what it rewards.

tests.answer: It signals that consumers want more, and higher profits give firms an incentive to produce more.
It signals that consumers want more.
